scenarioName: CHF Exacerbation — Nitro-Induced Hypotension in the Elderly

scenarioStory.history: Husband reports increasing shortness of breath and orthopnea over the past 6 hours, now unable to lie flat or speak in full sentences. Productive cough with pink, frothy sputum since roughly 3 AM. Husband states she missed her furosemide dose yesterday.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find an 81-year-old female in severe respiratory distress, tripod-sitting, with audible rales and pink frothy sputum. She is hypertensive and tachycardic, consistent with acute decompensated heart failure. → CPAP and high-dose nitro started: CPAP is applied and coached, and high-dose nitroglycerin is given for the severely hypertensive presentation. Initial response is favorable — oxygenation and work of breathing improve. → SBP reassessed before repeat nitro: Reassessment before the scheduled repeat nitroglycerin dose reveals the patient has become hypotensive — a known risk in this volume-depleted, diuretic-treated elderly patient. Further nitroglycerin is appropriately withheld. → Fluid bolus given for hypotension: Following the fluid bolus, blood pressure recovers while CPAP and oxygenation are maintained. Patient is packaged for transport with continuous reassessment.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Severe shortness of breath, unable to lie flat

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find an 81-year-old female in severe respiratory distress, tripod-sitting, with audible rales and pink frothy sputum. She is hypertensive and tachycardic, consistent with acute decompensated heart failure.

scenarioEvents.name: CPAP and high-dose nitro started
scenarioEvents.description: CPAP is applied and coached, and high-dose nitroglycerin is given for the severely hypertensive presentation. Initial response is favorable — oxygenation and work of breathing improve.
relatedChecklist: Apply CPAP for severe respiratory distress with hypoxia; coach patient through mask seal
Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL for SBP ≥160/MAP >120; may repeat every 5 min if SBP remains >100 mmHg

scenarioEvents.name: SBP reassessed before repeat nitro
scenarioEvents.description: Reassessment before the scheduled repeat nitroglycerin dose reveals the patient has become hypotensive — a known risk in this volume-depleted, diuretic-treated elderly patient. Further nitroglycerin is appropriately withheld.
relatedChecklist: Hold further nitroglycerin; SBP 92 mmHg is below the >100 mmHg threshold required to repeat
IV fluid bolus 250-500 mL for SBP <100 mmHg

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid bolus given for hypotension
scenarioEvents.description: Following the fluid bolus, blood pressure recovers while CPAP and oxygenation are maintained. Patient is packaged for transport with continuous reassessment.
relatedChecklist: Maintain continuous CPAP mask seal through transport; do not break seal until ED handoff
Reassess full vital signs and mental status serially en route

scenarioEvents.name: Nitro repeated without BP recheck
scenarioEvents.description: The crew repeats the nitroglycerin dose purely on the 5-minute timer without rechecking blood pressure first. Hypotension develops unrecognized and progresses further than it should have.
relatedChecklist: Norepinephrine 1.2 mcg/min IV (62 kg × 0.02 mcg/kg/min), titrate to SBP >90 mmHg

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid bolus withheld
scenarioEvents.description: The crew recognizes the hypotension but does not give the indicated fluid bolus. Perfusion continues to deteriorate.
relatedChecklist: IV fluid bolus 250-500 mL now indicated for worsening SBP <100 mmHg
